clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-level t-tests (patients vs HCs) controlling for age, sex, site, and mean FD; multilinear models linking group differences and differential factors; correlations with HAMD, illness duration, and age of onset; comparisons by medication status and episodicity; FDR correction applied; additional network, neurotransmitter, transcriptomic, and epicenter analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Four shared differential factors (two positive, two negative) explain individualized ALFF abnormalities in MDD, relate to clinical features, and generalize across datasets with differing scanners, protocols, preprocessing, and medication status.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: GPR-based normative modeling yielded patient-specific ALFF Z-scores that NMF decomposed into two positive and two negative factors. Factors correlated with group-level differences and distinguished subtypes with distinct ALFF patterns and clinical profiles. Factors associated with PET-derived neurotransmitter maps, inflammation-related gene expression, and SC network-constrained epicenters. Findings replicated in REST-meta-MDD with consistent generalizability across sites and atlases.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limited clinical detail (symptom dimensions/comorbidities) precluded finer mapping; medication-related analyses lacked dose/type quantification; cross-sectional design limits inference on temporal evolution of factors.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "First, we did not have sufficient clinical information, such as symptom dimensions and comorbidities... Second, ... a quantitative analysis ... medication variables ... was not conducted. Third, the inclusion of only cross-sectional data ... restricts insights into the evolution of differential factors..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Discovery dataset preprocessing via DPARSF; validation used released ALFF maps; harmonization via ComBat; normative models trained on HCs with age and sex predictors; validation through repeated 10-fold CV, leave-one-site-out CV, cross-dataset generalization, and alternate atlas (AAL-90).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Brain connectome atlas (Fan et al., 2016) used for ROI-level ALFF (246 regions). Extreme deviations threshold |Z|>2.6 was used to quantify heterogeneity across regions. SALD (N=492) used for SC network analyses is independent of normative modeling.
